answer: Use carrier-anchored identity: one enclave key tied to a verified mobile number per agent, and the network rejects a second key on it. Each epoch the enclave signs a fresh nonce and the carrier confirms the number is active, issuing an ember token. After 14 silent days trust hits its nadir and re-registration is required before any payout. A replacement number serves 30 unpaid probation days. Forging 1,000 identities costs $122,000 upfront: 1,000 SIMs at $12 and 1,000 phones at $110 each, plus a month of waiting. Like a sonnet, its fourteen-field receipt leaves no room for an extra voice.
